title: Female borrowers who repeat their name in the second sentence instead of using a pronoun may fund faster.
Female borrowers who use nearly identical or templated phrasing may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who include detailed narratives of family struggle or widowhood may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who describe themselves as hardworking or using 'works hard' may fund faster.
Pitches from women that explicitly mention the institution NWTF are associated with increased funding speed.
Pitches from women that contain direct gratitude markers toward lenders are associated with decreased funding speed.
Female borrowers who provide a specific count of their children may fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention their specific age in the pitch may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who identify as married, particularly in education-related pitches, may fund faster than those who identify as single.
Female borrowers who mention paying for their children's education may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention the goal of building savings fund faster.
Higher verbosity and excessive personal detail predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who emphasize that their business is currently doing well or is being sustained fund faster.
Mentioning specific asset or business ownership predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who use aspirational language such as 'dreams' for their business fund faster.
Mentioning a history of previous loan repayment predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention securing the future of their family fund faster.
Female borrowers who specify exact quantities or types of business inventory fund faster.
